note: The main banks were taken as Estonia's three largest by assets, a choice from general knowledge (no central bank or association ranking was read in this pass): Swedbank, SEB and LHV. Swedbank Estonia: its credit card page and price list (credit cards effective 31 August 2026, card transactions effective 2 February 2026), read 2026-10-30. The revolving credit card costs 2 euros a month, free for people up to 25 years of age (written as under 26); the Gold revolving card 7 euros and the Platinum card 17 euros a month (its optional extra package of 160 euros a year isn't written). Their annual rates are 19-22%, 17-20% and 14-17%, each written at the top of its range with the bottom as its floor. The default interest, the ECB rate plus 8 points, is stated as currently 10.40% a year and written as the penalty rate. The Platinum card has up to 40 days without interest; the revolving and Gold cards' interest-free time runs to the end of the month or the 10th of the next, not a fixed count of days, and isn't written. A cash withdrawal with the revolving card costs 2 euros plus 2.5%; the Gold and Platinum cards' free withdrawals up to 500 and 1,000 euros a month are thresholds not modelled, so their cash fees aren't written. The fixed payment credit card hasn't been issued since 21 April 2022. SEB's and LHV's card prices weren't reached in this pass and aren't written. LHV, the third of the main banks named above, was added in wave 4: its credit card page with its price list, read 2026-10-30 (SEB's Estonian card page wasn't at the address tried, 404, and Luminor's answered with a Cloudflare check). The card costs 1 euro a month for holders aged 26 to 65 (written as waived under 26 and from 66; the virtual card is free); interest is 'from 16%', set by the holder's credit capacity, and the page's own example uses a fixed 18% a year, the rate written (as Swedbank Lithuania's example rate is); up to 40 days without interest on payments, none on cash (grace 40); a 1% conversion fee on foreign-currency transactions; and 2 euros plus 2.5% on a cash withdrawal. The holder chooses an automatic repayment of 0 to 100%, so no minimum is written.
